method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (vrsa-core.l4, with four regulative rules) and a seat layer of 17 exported questions (vrsa-seat.l4) that restates no rule (since finding 25 the recognition question takes the primary victim from the core's s 20 rule, and the core gives recognition payments only for an act of violence or act of modern slavery); no REFUSE (the Regulation cl 9 weekly rate answers an explicit not-covered value, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Victims Rights and Support Act 2013 No 37 (act-2013-037), corpus document nsw_legislation:2025-02-01/act-2013-037 (version date 2025-02-01, scraped 2025-03-10), deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2013-037.txt; with the Victims Rights and Support Regulation 2019 (sl-2019-0398), corpus document nsw_legislation:2025-02-01/sl-2019-0398 (version date 2025-02-01, scraped 2025-03-10), deposited at ../../../victims-rights-and-support-regulation-2019/registers/source-bundle/sl-2019-0398.txt; both from the Open Australian Legal Corpus version 7.1.0 (NSW Legislation collected 10 March 2025). NOT THE CURRENT OFFICIAL TEXT; IT MAY BE OUT OF DATE. The amounts are those fixed in the deposited Regulation (cl 5, 8, 10-14), encoded as stated.

seat: the victim applying for support (a primary, secondary or family victim, or the parent, step-parent or guardian caring for a child primary victim)
seats: the victim applying for support (a primary, secondary or family victim, or the parent, step-parent or guardian caring for a child primary victim)
regulative_rules: s 40(1)-(3), (5), (7): the application for financial support or a recognition payment must be duly made within the time allowed (2 years after the act or after a child victim turns 18; 2 years after a later-established cause of death; 10 years for a recognition payment involving domestic violence, child abuse or sexual assault; no limit under s 40(7))
s 43(1), (4): the Commissioner must determine a duly made application and give written notice
s 40(6): claims may be made under the application until 5 years pass or the total maximum is given, and not after
s 54(2): the Commissioner must pay a claim, subject to the conditions of the approval
scope: IN: Act Part 4 ss 18, 19 (19(3A) worked out in the rule; the 19(3), (8) meaning of violent conduct, sexual assault and domestic violence, glossed in the violent-conduct @desc), 19A, 19AB, 20 (including rescuers), 21 (witness; parent or guardian of a child victim who later learns of the act), 22 (family victim, immediate family, de facto partner after 2 years), 23, 24, 25 (court compensation; motor accidents with the (2A) and (2B) exceptions; own offence; family of the alleged road-crime offender with the (3A) exception; convicted inmates unless special circumstances), 26-29A with the cross-reductions in ss 26(2) and 27(2), 30(2), 30A, 34-36 (every category only in respect of an act of violence or act of modern slavery), 38, 39, 40, 43(1) and (4) (regulative: determination and written notice), 47, 53 (suspension pending review, as a fact), 54(2) (regulative); Regulation cl 4 (as the counselling class), 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. NOT COVERED (asserted): Regulation cl 9, the weekly rate of actual loss of earnings (pre-2012 Workers Compensation Act 1987 s 37, indexed; not deposited); the weekly rate is an input capped by cl 10(3)(a) and 11(2)(a). OUT: Part 2 (Charter), Part 3 (Commissioner, Fund), Part 5 (restitution by offenders; no offender seat), Part 6 (court compensation, except as the s 25(1) exclusion), ss 41, 41A, 42, 43(2), (3), (5)-(7), 44, 45, 46, 48, 49-52, 55, 56, Parts 7-9; Regulation cl 6, 15, 16.
